metadata.scope: Servo brackets, servo horns, robot arm links, wheel hubs, gripper fingers, chassis plates.

material_suggestions.use_case: functional servo brackets and arm links
material_suggestions.notes: Best printed option; resists flex fatigue better than PETG.
Easy to print; use metal inserts for servo mounting holes.

parts.name: MG996R servo bracket (U-bracket)

fit_guidance_mm.servo_gap: servo body clears wing inner face by ≥2 mm each side in X

tab_span.note: center-to-center of MG996R mounting holes along X

bracket_t.note: wall thickness; wing centered on tab hole so hole drills through full thickness

tab_hole_z.note: MG996R mounting hole height above servo body base

wing_w.note: wing Y-span = servo width + two wall thicknesses = 28.5 mm

wing_h.note: wing height above base plate = 48 mm; servo top sits flush or below wing top

plate_l.note: base plate X-length; outer wing face at ±(tab_span/2 + bracket_t/2) = ±26.5 mm

main_features: two vertical wing plates centered at x = ±tab_span/2 — hold the servo mounting tabs
servo mounting tab holes through wings along X axis at tab_hole_z above base
cable relief hole in base plate center
four base mounting holes in 2×2 pattern for attaching bracket to robot frame
design_rules: Wings are centered at x = ±tab_span/2 (±24.5 mm). Each wing is bracket_t thick, wing_w wide in Y, wing_h tall in Z (above base plate). The servo body slides into the open top of the U between the two wings.
Tab holes pass through wings along the X axis: use rotate([0,90,0]) cylinder at translate([±tab_span/2, 0, bracket_t + tab_hole_z]).
Base plate: plate_l × wing_w × bracket_t, centered at z = bracket_t/2. plate_l = tab_span + bracket_t so the plate reaches the outer faces of both wings.
Wings sit on top of the base plate — translate wing cube to z = bracket_t + wing_h/2 so wing bottom edge is at z = bracket_t.
No servo pocket cutout is needed. The servo body (servo_l=40.5 mm) fits in the open space between the wing inner faces (gap = tab_span − bracket_t = 45 mm). The servo slides in from the top.
Do NOT place tab holes as vertical cylinders through the base plate — that drills in the wrong direction.
Do NOT put wing plates along Y (front/back of servo) — wings must be at x = ±tab_span/2 so the holes align with the servo's mounting tabs.
Do NOT center the servo pocket at z = 0 — it will destroy the base plate.
validation_criteria: two wing cubes, each centered at x = ±tab_span/2, with Z translation = bracket_t + wing_h/2
tab holes use rotate([0,90,0]) cylinder — NOT rotate([90,0,0]) and NOT unrotated Z cylinders
tab hole Z position = bracket_t + tab_hole_z ≈ 13.5 mm above ground
base plate cube in union with Z translation = bracket_t/2
no minkowski() or subtracted servo pocket cube
failure_modes: tab holes drilled vertically through base plate (wrong axis) — servo cannot be bolted in
wing plates placed at y = ±(servo_w/2 + bracket_t/2) along Y — holes do not align with MG996R tabs
servo pocket centered at z = 0 — destroys base plate
wings placed at outer extremes of plate as thin end-caps (base_extend trick) — no structural hold on servo
tab holes at z = 0 — holes below base plate surface

constraint_checks.message: Wings must be at x = ±tab_span/2 so tab holes align with MG996R mounting holes.

constraint_checks.expression: rotate([0,90,0]) before cylinder for tab holes
constraint_checks.message: Tab holes must drill along X, not Z.
Tab holes must be at the correct height above the base plate.
